summary: Applying SMOTE to the training data before fitting a default RandomForestClassifier() does not meaningfully change minority-class (>50K) F1: the single-split difference was +0.006 and the repeated-CV mean difference was +0.001, both far below the 0.02 threshold.
primary_metric_name: F1(>50K) difference, SMOTE minus no-resampling (mean over 20 CV folds)
direction: no practically significant change (|diff| << 0.02); SMOTE effect is negligible/inconsistent in sign across folds
methodological_choices: One-hot encoded all categorical columns (drop_first=False), filled missing categorical values (NaN, originally '?') with an explicit 'Missing' category rather than dropping rows or mode-imputing; no scaling (tree-based model). Target encoded as 1 for '>50K'. Primary comparison used one stratified 75/25 train/test split (random_state=42): RandomForestClassifier() fit on raw training data vs. on SMOTE-resampled training data (imblearn default k_neighbors=5), both scored on the identical untouched test fold using F1 with '>50K' as positive class. Both RF and SMOTE used fully default hyperparameters as specified by H5.
verification_method: 20x repeated stratified 5-fold CV (RepeatedStratifiedKFold, 5 splits x 4 repeats), varying the random seed per fold for both RandomForestClassifier and SMOTE, computing the plain-vs-SMOTE F1 difference on each fold and a 95% CI on the mean difference.
verification_result: Held up: mean diff across 20 folds = +0.0009 (F1 plain mean=0.6703, sd=0.0084; F1 SMOTE mean=0.6713, sd=0.0081), 95% CI [-0.0007, 0.0026], entirely within +/-0.02 and straddling zero. Per-fold differences ranged from -0.0083 to +0.0087, flipping sign across folds, confirming no stable or practically meaningful effect of SMOTE on F1 for this model/dataset combination.
